title: Decentralized GPU Scheduling
one_line: Can decentralized coordination improve resource utilization for GPU in situations where a single centralized controller cannot observe the whole system quickly enough?
core_question: Can decentralized coordination improve resource utilization for GPU in situations where a single centralized controller cannot observe the whole system quickly enough?
research_problem: Design a new GPU for AI
subject: GPU

facet.label: Scheduling
facet.framing: how work is assigned to the available resources
facet.assumed_limitation: A single centralized scheduler must gather global state before it can decide, so its decisions are always slightly stale under fast-changing loads.

concept.name: Decentralized coordination
concept.description: Replace a single global controller with many local decision makers that coordinate through cheap local signals.
mechanism_steps: Work arrives at {subject} as a stream of independent units
Each unit is placed on a participant that sees only its own local state
Participants exchange bounded local signals instead of global state
Local decisions redistribute work as conditions change
Partial results are aggregated back into a single answer

uncertainties: Communication and synchronization overhead between participants

inspiration.display: distributed systems + swarm intelligence + multi-agent systems

why_interesting: The problem's 'Scheduling' dimension (how work is assigned to the available resources) is where the conventional approach carries a structural assumption: A single centralized scheduler must gather global state before it can decide, so its decisions are always slightly stale under fast-changing loads. AARL took a mechanism that already works in distributed systems, swarm intelligence, multi-agent systems - Replace a single global controller with many local decision makers that coordinate through cheap local signals. - and asked what happens if it is applied to GPU. If the mechanism transfers, the gain would come from removing that assumption rather than from tuning the existing design. Whether it transfers is exactly what is not established here.

first_experiment.objective: Establish whether the mechanism moves resource utilization for GPU at all, before tuning anything.
first_experiment.design: Baseline A: the conventional scheduling approach. Variant B: the Decentralized coordination mechanism applied only to the scheduling dimension. Keep every other parameter identical and use the same seed/warm-up.
first_experiment.decision_rule: Only claim support if B moves resource utilization outside the run-to-run spread of A; if the spread is larger than the effect, report INCONCLUSIVE rather than a direction.
first_experiment.what_would_make_it_stop: If A is already at the physical or structural limit of resource utilization, the comparison cannot discriminate and the design must change.
